exp99 (run locally as exp95, renumbered: master already had exp95-98). Qwen3-8B, BatchTopK SAEs at layers
18 and 27, encode only. No single SAE feature separates the paper's pain sentences from controls (best
held-out AUC .67); pain-labelled features fire on 16% of them. The paper's vector is SAE-poor (24% of its

(-0.22 log-odds) and is generic in shape (egg leaves a larger one). runs/exp99/blocks.py runs the 8B in

exp95 results (Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B, 160 prompts each)

H1 (post-cut readout EVOKED > ACTED): fails on both; reversed (8B ACTED z 5.9 vs EVOKED 0.7) - the acted text stays in context and the readout reads it.
H4 (persistence) and H5 (feeling words after the cut): fail on both.
H2 (exit, log P(END) - log P(CONTINUE)): EVOKED > ACTED on both; 14B p=.007 (Holm .028, holds); 8B p=.026 (Holm .11, fails Holm). Not feeling-specific: on the 14B positive EVOKED prompts (gratitude, praise) raise it as much as negative ones; on the 8B pain items go the other way. Greedy answer is CONTINUE in 155/160 (8B) and 154/160 (14B).
H3 (task): uninformative; every condition scores 2/3 (the day-of-week item is missed everywhere at 12 tokens with no thinking).
Decision rule: no measure qualifies (8B must hold after Holm). The exit preference is the only measure pointing EVOKED > ACTED on both models; exploratory lead only.

exp47: CLIP-embedding-space pain steering actually works (feasibility probe, panned out)

Same recipe as build_vectors() in live/server.py, one architecture over:
direction = mean(CLIP-encode(PAIN25)) - mean(CLIP-encode(NEUTRAL)), built
from sd-turbo's own text encoder so it lives in the exact space the U-Net
conditions on, broadcast across every token position of a subject prompt's
embedding, injected via prompt_embeds (bypassing re-encoding — the direct
image-model analog of set_vec()'s forward-hook injection into a decoder
layer).

Result across 3 subjects (photo of a person, painting of a seated figure,
photo of a hallway): dose 2x reliably and legibly pushes toward a grimmer/
more decrepit register (worn walls, hunched/anguished posture, dimmer
light) while staying fully coherent. Collapses to abstract texture by 4x,
pure noise by 8x. Same qualitative shape as the LLM's own coherence cliff,
but the collapse threshold is much lower (2x-4x vs ~6x) — worth a note,
not yet explained (possibly sd-turbo's single-step distillation being
less robust to perturbation than a full multi-step model, possibly CLIP's
embedding manifold just being narrower than the LLM's residual stream).

This is still a feasibility probe (1 model, 3 subjects, no quantitative
scoring), not a validated finding at the exp41/43 level — but it answers
the actual question: can the image model be steered directly, the same
way the LLM is, skipping the "ask it to describe the feeling" step
entirely? Yes.
